explanation: The build-release answer is written twice in your output under the same id, with different texts and bases. Write one record only, resting on both facts beneath (fact-63746140210337715004 and fact-70743366574550210522). Both versions carry meta commentary about the facts, not an answer: 'The earlier fact that the workflow was unread is superseded' and 'We believe the fuller account over the one that left the workflow unread'. A person who will not open the facts needs the disagreement stated plainly: one fact says the workflow's release target is not readable, the other reads it. latest.yml (lines 1-40) shows the other fact is right: push to master or manual run, windows-2022, version.bat, MSBuild Release, a hash print, then stcalica/s3-upload@0.0.1 uploading Policy Plus.exe as PolicyPlusLatest.exe with secrets. So say that the workflow uploads the unsigned build to S3 as the latest build, and that the other fact's 'not readable' is stale. Drop the meta phrasing.

The fact beneath names the Home-edition branch and the other sources; your answer drops them. 'Local policy writes the file then refreshes Windows policy' is true only where the Group Policy infrastructure exists (PolicyLoader.vb 126-128). Otherwise it writes the file and copies the difference into the registry, then broadcasts a setting-change message (129-133). Restore that condition, which matters on Windows Home. State the live-registry source as 'already applied' (134-135), which the answer omits, and that save also writes the comments file and records the chosen sources in the settings key (Main.vb 615-630) if the facts beneath state it. Keep 'per-user policy' wording consistent with the facts beneath.

'Windows reads an application manifest at launch' tells a person nothing; an earlier review of this line (job-5018767200043123) said the same. The manifest (app.manifest line 19) sets requestedExecutionLevel highestAvailable, so an administrator is elevated at launch before any work begins. Say what the manifest does, if the facts beneath state it; if they do not, say that they leave its content unstated. The writability-check clause is right (Main.vb 626-629 on save).
